newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sanyo Sec's capital ratio at 164.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sanyo Sec's capital ratio at 164.4 pct.

text.p: Sanyo Securities Co Ltd said on Thursday that its capital safety ratio stood at 164.4 percent at the end of March 1997, down from 170.7 percent a year ago.
Japan's Securities and Exchange Law requires brokerages to disclose the ratio, which indicates their financial health.
The ratio is that of net capital and latent profits on securities holdings against risk assets and possible losses from the securities business.

A ratio of below 150 percent is considered an early warning level and if the ratio falls below 120 percent, financial authorities can order brokerages to improve their operations under the Securities and Exchange Law.

Sanyo also said in a statement that it held problem loans totalling some 80 billion yen to four affiliates and that it made no financial assistance to the affiliates in the financial year which ended on March 31.

A Sanyo official told reporters that the brokerage had provided 8.3 billion yen worth of financial assistance to affiliates in the past three years, which was much smaller than the brokerage had originally planned.
